subject.title: Next Sprint B: model-input validation guardrails

question: Should configured model `input` accept audio/video as valid provider metadata while adding semantic guardrails, or should OpenClaw reject those modalities from configured chat models by default?
rationale: Current main deliberately accepts audio/video in config but still narrows other runtime paths and trusts user-declared image capability, so automation cannot choose the permanent API contract without breaking one side of existing behavior.

options.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
options.body: Keep audio/video as valid model metadata, then add trusted catalog/provider cross-checks and clear diagnostics for unsupported runtime use.

options.title: Reject unsupported inputs by default
options.body: Tighten configured model validation to fail unsupported modalities, with migration or override handling for existing multimodal configs.

options.title: Defer contract change
options.body: Leave current behavior in place until generated-catalog widening and media-output policy are settled together.

recommendation.title: Accept metadata plus guardrails
recommendation.body: Keep audio/video as valid model metadata, then add trusted catalog/provider cross-checks and clear diagnostics for unsupported runtime use.

likelyOwner.reason: They have recent merged history on configured model resolution and adjacent model discovery/media capability paths, making them the best routing candidate for the API/product contract choice.
